messages.subject: Convert Arabic numerals to words
messages.body_plain:
coRpus linguists,

I'm trying to automate the conversion of Arabic numerals to words (with the goal of determining the final phoneme in that number with the help of a POS tagger [FreeLing] that can also output phonemes, once I have the orthographic representation). For example, I'd like to convert, say, "500" to "five hundred" or "34" to "thirty four". Actually, in my case, I'd like to get the Spanish words ("quinientos", "treinta y cuatro"), which I could do, in a worse case scenario, with the "translate" package if I can get the English words. A search on Google didn't return anything obvious (to me) that does this in R.

The as.roman() function is great for converting between Arabic and Roman numerals, but I don't see anything that does this with words.

Does anyone see a way of doing this, short of writing a find and replace function from zero to infinity?

convertNumToWord <- function(text) {
  text <- gsub("\\b0\\b", "zero", text)
  text <- gsub("\\b1\\b", "one", text)
  text <- gsub("\\b2\\b", "two", text)
  text <- gsub("\\b3\\b", "three", text)
  # etc. to infinity :)
  return(text)
}

Thanks in advance for any ideas.

messages.subject: Locating EOF files
messages.body_plain:
Having trouble with some corpus files. They need to be read in with quote='"' but some files give me 'EOF within quoted string' errors. It's the same files each time, yet when I go back to the purchased CD and extract them again, the new directory will have different files which will consistently give me EOF errors. Gotta be hardware as it's only this one computer. Have tried extracting again, copying good extracted corpus directory from one computer to another, but always some errors.

Anyway, my question is this: since R doesn't crash on EOF errors but just loads the file anyway and then gives the 50+ warnings() message, is there a way I can get R to record which files have the errors? Something like this:

EOF<-c()
for(file in 1:length(file.names)){
current<-scan(file.names[file],what='char',sep='\n',quote='"',quiet=T)
if(eof.error){       #not a real command of course.
EOF<-c(EOF,file)
}
}

Alternatively, is there a way to get R to break when it encounters these files?

I can locate them manually by using Nim strategy, but there are over 50 of them. I can also approximate my script above by recording which files have nchar() outliers.

At least if I can get a list of all bad files, I can maybe compile a working version from different directories and use the corpus on this machine.

--
Kevin Parent, Ph.D
Korea Maritime University

Thanks for tryCatch. To answer Alex's question about what I want to do, it's basically just troubleshooting, trying to figure out why I'm getting this problem. (That's also why I used a file counter instead of for(file in file.names)--because I kept altering that line to for(file in 4000:length(file.names)), etc. to locate the problem files.) However, Mac's message that he's experienced the same issue changes things.

Mac, R 3.1.0 and Windows 8?

Mac also asked if the issue was really affecting the outcome. Yes and no. I only get the error when scan is set to quote=(double quotation marks) AND sep='\n'. Change either parameter and it generally works, albeit not in the format I want.  If I ignore the warnings, I end up in a couple cases with corpus lines over 2 million characters long.

I can do: paste(scan(etc),collapse=' ') and then strsplit back to where I want it. My problems are first, that strsplit is slow over the course of 4000+ files, and second, I shouldn't *have* to do this in the first place.

I've officially had enough of Win8. When I first bought this machine I tried installing Linux but ran into all that secure boot BS. After two days I had a laptop that couldn't boot to anything, not even the emergency settings nor the USB (it has no CD drive) and the store I bought it from gave me a new one and I was afraid to do it again. But enough is enough.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Kevin,
I have R 3.0.2 and Windows 7 64-bit.

On 22/06/2014 10:39 PM, Kevin Parent wrote:

> Thanks for tryCatch. To answer Alex's question about what I want to do, it's basically just troubleshooting, trying to figure out why I'm getting this problem. (That's also why I used a file counter instead of for(file in file.names)--because I kept altering that line to for(file in 4000:length(file.names)), etc. to locate the problem files.) However, Mac's message that he's experienced the same issue changes things.
>
> Mac, R 3.1.0 and Windows 8?
>
> Mac also asked if the issue was really affecting the outcome. Yes and no. I only get the error when scan is set to quote=(double quotation marks) AND sep='\n'. Change either parameter and it generally works, albeit not in the format I want.  If I ignore the warnings, I end up in a couple cases with corpus lines over 2 million characters long.
>
> I can do: paste(scan(etc),collapse=' ') and then strsplit back to where I want it. My problems are first, that strsplit is slow over the course of 4000+ files, and second, I shouldn't *have* to do this in the first place.
>
> I've officially had enough of Win8. When I first bought this machine I tried installing Linux but ran into all that secure boot BS. After two days I had a laptop that couldn't boot to anything, not even the emergency settings nor the USB (it has no CD drive) and the store I bought it from gave me a new one and I was afraid to do it again. But enough is enough.
>
>
>
> On Mon, Jun 23, 2014 at 1:16 AM, Mac Salt <stygi...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > I started getting the EOF error after upgrading R 6 months ago. The files (which also had double quotes and the quote character) gave me no problems before the upgrade but gave me this error afterward. They were otherwise processed fine, same as before. Are you sure the error is affecting your files or your analysis?
> > On Jun 22, 2014 11:59 AM, "Alex Perrone" <boet...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Have you tried tryCatch?  Then on the warning, add the filename to your vector.
> > > P.S. What do you plan to do with the broken files? What's causing it? Maybe you can solve it directly by pre-processing step with readLines...
> > > P.P.S. Minor: your 'file' variable is misleading as it's an index variable. If file.names is a vector, you can directly do: for (file in file.names) { scan(file, ... ) }
> > >
> > >
> > > On Sun, Jun 22, 2014 at 2:04 AM, Kevin Parent <kspa...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > Sorry for the continued updates. I did find that options(warn=2) will break on the EOF errors, and setting it to 1 will print the message as it occurs but still continue. But given the sheer number of these problem files, recording the problem files into a vector would still be much more useful.
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > On Sun, Jun 22, 2014 at 2:31 PM, Kevin Parent <kspa...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > For clarity's sake, they should be read with quote = (double quotation mark). That didn't come out well in gmail.
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > On Sun, Jun 22, 2014 at 2:28 PM, Kevin Parent <kspa...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > Having trouble with some corpus files. They need to be read in with quote='"' but some files give me 'EOF within quoted string' errors. It's the same files each time, yet when I go back to the purchased CD and extract them again, the new directory will have different files which will consistently give me EOF errors. Gotta be hardware as it's only this one computer. Have tried extracting again, copying good extracted corpus directory from one computer to another, but always some errors.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Anyway, my question is this: since R doesn't crash on EOF errors but just loads the file anyway and then gives the 50+ warnings() message, is there a way I can get R to record which files have the errors? Something like this:
> > > > > >
> > > > > > EOF<-c()
> > > > > > for(file in 1:length(file.names)){
> > > > > > current<-scan(file.names[file],what='char',sep='\n',quote='"',quiet=T)
> > > > > > if(eof.error){       #not a real command of course.
> > > > > > EOF<-c(EOF,file)
> > > > > > }
> > > > > > }
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Alternatively, is there a way to get R to break when it encounters these files?
> > > > > >
> > > > > > I can locate them manually by using Nim strategy, but there are over 50 of them. I can also approximate my script above by recording which files have nchar() outliers.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > At least if I can get a list of all bad files, I can maybe compile a working version from different directories and use the corpus on this machine.
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > --
> > > > > > Kevin Parent, Ph.D
> > > > > > Korea Maritime University
